name: Gallifrey Falls // No More
oracle_text:
Gallifrey Falls deals 4 damage to each creature. If a creature dealt damage this way would die this turn, exile it instead.
Fuse (You may cast one or both halves of this card from your hand.)
blocked_sentences: Gallifrey Falls deals 4 damage to each creature. If a creature dealt damage this way would die this turn, exile it instead

needs.what: split cards: one card with two independently castable halves, each with its own mana cost, plus Fuse -- "you may cast one or both halves of this card from your hand", casting both as a single spell. The catalog row is layout='split', type_line='Instant // Instant', mana_cost='{4}{R}{R} // {2}{W}', keywords='Fuse'.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: docs/rules-coverage.md:157 lists split and adventure cards as not implemented, separately from modal double-faced cards. There is no concept of casting half a card: `mana_cost` is one string and `spell_effects` is one list. Unlike an MDFC, gate 3 here must consume BOTH halves' printed text from a single catalog row. The authoring pipeline emits exactly one card entry per answer file (`collect_answers` reads `answer["card"]` as a single dict), and a double-faced card is two card entries linked by `back_face`. Gate 3 compounds it: `collect_answers` looks the oracle text up by the payload's name, and a front face authored under its own name misses the catalog's joined "A // B" row. The repo's existing two-faced cards (bloodline_keeper / lord_of_lineage) are hand-written in data/cards/ for exactly this reason.
